title: 2D target search with boundary-induced resetting
abstract: Most studies of stochastic search processes with resetting focus on spontaneous resetting events that occur at a random sequence of times typically generated by a Poisson process. One of the major consequences of spontaneous resetting is that it yields a finite mean first passage time (MFPT) in unbounded domains, resulting in an optimal resetting rate that minimises the MFPT. An optimal resetting rate can also occur in bounded domains provided that the reset point is not too far from the target. Recently, there has been growing interest in event-based rather than spontaneous resetting, where resetting is triggered when a specific threshold is reached. Identifying the threshold with a physical non-target boundary then leads to so-called boundary-induced resetting. In this paper, we explore the effects of boundary-induced resetting on single-particle diffusive search in a two-dimensional (2D) bounded domain $Ω$ containing one or more small interior targets. The interior target boundaries are totally absorbing, whereas the exterior boundary $\partial Ω$ is sticky. That is, whenever the particle reaches a point on $\partial Ω$ it remains attached for a random waiting time $τ$ after which it immediately resets to a fixed interior point $\x_0\in Ω$. Using renewal theory, matched asymptotic analysis and Green's functions we calculate the unconditional MFPT for absorption by any of the targets and compare this with the corresponding MFPT of a search process on the same domain with a reflecting surface $\partial Ω$ and no resetting. We show that boundary-induced resetting only reduces the MFPT relative to the no resetting case if the searcher's reset point $\x_0$ is sufficiently close to one of the targets.
summary: This paper analyzes the Mean First Passage Time for diffusion in a bounded 2D domain subjected to boundary-induced resetting. It compares this time to the case without resetting, showing that the benefit of resetting is highly dependent on the geometry and the proximity of the reset point to the target. The methodology combines renewal theory with advanced asymptotic analysis.
main_problem: The paper investigates how boundary-induced resetting affects the Mean First Passage Time (MFPT) for a particle diffusing in a bounded 2D domain containing absorbing targets.
main_result: Boundary-induced resetting only reduces the MFPT compared to a reflecting boundary if the particle's reset point is sufficiently close to the target(s), unlike some simpler 1D cases.
method: The analysis employs renewal theory, matched asymptotic expansions, and Green's functions to calculate the unconditional MFPT.
model_or_system: The model is single-particle diffusion in a 2D bounded domain ($\Omega$) with absorbing interior targets and a sticky exterior boundary ($\partial\Omega$) that causes resetting to a fixed interior point $x_0$.
key_observables: Unconditional Mean First Passage Time (MFPT) for absorption by any target.
important_parameters: The mean waiting time ($	au$) at the sticky boundary, the initial position ($x_0$), and the geometry of the domain ($\Omega$) and targets.
main_assumptions: Targets are assumed to be small and well-separated from each other and the exterior boundary; the analysis often relies on approximations for the leading order behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate contour plots showing the MFPT and the sign of the benefit function ($\chi$) for single and dumbbell target configurations in 2D, comparing resetting effects in 1D vs 2D.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the simpler 1D interval case, then generalizes the methodology to the 2D domain $\Omega$, deriving the necessary renewal equations and calculating the MFPT using advanced mathematical techniques.
why_interesting: The study provides a rigorous theoretical framework for non-equilibrium dynamics in confined spaces, which is relevant for understanding transport phenomena in mesoscopic systems or engineered quantum environments.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic illustration of a sample path of a Brownian particle in [0, L] with a non-absorbing sticky boundary at x = L and an absorbing target at x = 0. The particle hits x = L twice prior to finding the target. In each case the particle sticks to the boundary for a random waiting time τj, j = 1, 2, after which it desorbs and immediately resets to its initial position x0.
Figure 2. MFPT T(x0) given by equation (2.17) plotted on a log-scale with D, L = 1. The MFPT blows up as x0 →L for all τ > 0.

Figure 3. MFPT T(x0) with boundary resetting and a sticky boundary at x = L for various mean waiting times τ. The dashed curve shows the classical MFPT T0(x0) without resetting and a reflecting boundary at x = L. We take D = L = 1 in all cases so that τD = 1/2. It can be seen that for τ < τD boundary resetting is advantageous in some part of the domain, but for τ > τD, no choice of x0 makes boundary resetting worthwhile.

Figure 4. Particle diffusing in a singularly perturbed domain Ω⊂R2 containing N totally absorbing interior compartments Uj centred at the positions xj, j = 1, . . . , N. The particle resets to its initial position x0 whenever it desorbs from the exterior boundary ∂Ω.

Figure 5. Polar contour plots of the MFPT T(x0; x1) given by equation (5.3) as a function of x0 = (a cos θ, a sin θ) for different target locations x1 = (b, 0) and τ = 0. The colouring of each plot is on a log-scale. Other parameters are D = 1 and ν = 0.2. Top left: b = 0; Top right: b = 0.3; Bottom left: b = 0.7; Bottom right: b = 0.95. The figure is generated using a discretization in polar coordinates, with a 50-point radial grid taken from 0.001 to 0.995, which accounts for singularities and blowups, and a 60-point angular grid taken from 0 to 2π.
